rows.note: Gaussian linear mixed-effects model fitted by REML to day_14_weight (grams) for 2,801 chicks in experimentally enlarged or reduced broods; 919 chicks in unmanipulated broods were excluded because those broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Fixed effects were the enlarged-versus-reduced indicator and categorical hatch year. Crossed random intercepts represented 332 rearing nests and 377 hatch/natal nests. No post-treatment brood-size, survival, derived condition-index, or incompletely recorded manipulation-magnitude variables were included. Native effect = -1.0784179574 g, SE = 0.0939358926 g; Wald z = -11.4803609900; inferential df not applicable because inference used the asymptotic Wald z distribution. Observation unit: chick measured at day 14. Design: brood-size manipulation with cross-fostering, comparing enlarged against reduced rearing broods.
rows.predictor: Indicator coded 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the adjusted mean day-14 weight contrast enlarged minus reduced.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Fitted OLS among experimentally enlarged and reduced rearing broods only, with fixed effects for the enlarged-versus-reduced indicator, categorical hatch_year, and linear realized post-treatment d14_rear_nest_brood_size. Thus the focal coefficient is a conditional/direct contrast at equal realized day-14 brood size, not the total assignment effect. Unmanipulated broods (rear_nest_trt=7) and rows missing fitted variables were excluded; fitted n=2,801 individual chicks. Observation unit: chick alive and measured at day 14. Design: brood-size manipulation with cross-fostering. Uncertainty: finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust covariance by 332 rearing nests and 377 hatch nests. Test: t=-7.80982405684161 with conservative inferential df=min(332,377)-1=331; two-sided p=7.634705371998944e-14. Native effect and SE are in grams.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced = 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) was modeled for 2,716 individual chicks in experimentally manipulated rearing broods (treatment codes 5 or 6) having a recorded nonzero net manipulation and complete weight, year, rearing-nest ID, and natal-nest ID. Unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. The fitted model was OLS with fixed breeding-year indicators and a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest and natal nest. There were 319 rearing nests and 363 natal nests. The focal test was t = -11.8194317926 with conservative inferential df = min(319, 363) - 1 = 318 (two-sided p = 5.73778843971e-27). Observation unit: individual chick measured at day 14. Design: experimental brood-size-manipulation dose analysis. The estimate and SE are in the native model scale of grams per one additional chick; no effect-size conversion was applied. Realized day-14 brood size and other post-treatment variables were not adjusted for.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: recorded net number of chicks added to the rearing brood, positive for additions and negative for removals; focal coefficient is the linear change in day-14 weight per one-chick increase

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length in millimetres. Fitted an OLS marginal model among chicks in experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods: day_14_tarsus_length ~ enlarged + categorical hatch_year. The focal indicator was 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged) and 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced); unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7 broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. No post-treatment variables were adjusted for. Uncertainty used an inclusion-exclusion two-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest and hatch nest, with finite-cluster corrections. Native effect=-0.3683072326 mm; SE=0.0388297915 mm; two-sided cluster-robust t=-9.4851715175; inferential df=331, defined as min(332 rearing-nest clusters, 377 hatch-nest clusters)-1; fitted n=2801 chicks. Observation unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14. Design: experimental enlarged-versus-reduced rearing-brood comparison with breeding-year fixed effects and two-way clustering by rearing and natal nest.
rows.predictor: Indicator equal to 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood; more sibling competition) and 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood; less sibling competition); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced.

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) modeled for 2,801 chicks in experimentally enlarged or reduced broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Chick-level OLS included breeding-year fixed effects. Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by rearing nest (332 clusters) and natal/hatch nest (377 clusters), rather than random intercepts. Native-scale focal effect = -1.016140 g, SE = 0.085665 g; t = -11.861778 with conservative inferential df = min(332,377)-1 = 331. Observation unit: chick. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed as an enlarged-versus-reduced contrast. No post-treatment brood-size, survival, derived condition-index, or manipulation-magnitude adjustment was used.
rows.predictor: Indicator equal to 1 for an experimentally enlarged rearing brood (rear_nest_trt=5) and 0 for an experimentally reduced rearing brood (rear_nest_trt=6); coefficient is adjusted mean day-14 weight for enlarged minus reduced broods

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) modeled by chick-level OLS among 3,679 complete cases from 447 rearing nests and 491 natal nests. The model included the ordered assigned-competition score, breeding-year fixed indicators, centered pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size, and centered rearing-nest hatch date. Two-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance accounted for dependence within rearing nests and natal nests. The focal test was t = -12.29789976300073 with inferential df = 446, defined conservatively as the smaller cluster count minus one; two-sided p = 3.919221613822266e-30. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear trend across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods; inclusion of the unmatched unmanipulated group is addressed by baseline covariate adjustment, but the focal coefficient assumes a linear trend across categories. Forty-one chicks were excluded for missing required clutch-size or hatch-date values.
rows.predictor: One-unit increase in ordered assigned sibling-competition score, constructed from rear_nest_trt as reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, and enlarged (code 5) = +1; coefficient is grams of day-14 weight per one-category increase

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) analyzed for 2,801 chicks in 332 experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods; unmatched unmanipulated broods were excluded. Chick-level OLS included breeding-year fixed effects. Uncertainty used a finite-sample-corrected one-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest, the treatment-assignment and shared-competition unit. Native-scale test: t = -11.35391099051849 with 331 inferential df (332 rearing-nest clusters minus 1); fitted n = 2,801 chicks. Observation unit: chick. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation. The estimate is the adjusted mean day-14 weight difference in grams, enlarged minus reduced.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced = 1 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GEE for day-14 weight (grams), fitted to 2,794 chicks from 331 experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched. Complete cases were required for weight, treatment, hatch year, rearing-nest hatch date, pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size, and rearing-nest ID. Fixed adjustment terms were a linear breeding-season trend (hatch_year minus its minimum), rearing-nest hatch date centered within breeding year, and pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size centered over the fitted sample. Exchangeable working correlation modeled dependence among chicks sharing a rearing nest, with robust sandwich SE (estimated working correlation 0.5390). No post-treatment covariates were included. Test statistic: t = -11.894606; inferential df = 326, defined as 331 rearing-nest clusters minus 5 fitted parameters. Observation unit: chick. Design: randomized rearing-brood-size manipulation comparing enlarged with reduced broods. The estimate is the adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in mean day-14 weight on the model's native gram scale.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced = 1 if rear_nest_trt == 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood; more sibling competition), and 0 if rear_nest_trt == 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

rows.note: Native outcome scale: grams of day-14 chick weight. Test: t = -6.935169419106875 with 242 inferential df (243 rearing-nest clusters minus 1); two-sided p = 3.675055886498829e-11. Fitted n = 2,334 chicks; observation unit = chick. Design/model: brood-size manipulation study analyzed with chick-level OLS; sample restricted to experimentally enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5) and unmanipulated (rear_nest_trt=7) rearing broods, excluding reduced broods and rows missing model variables. Fixed adjustment terms were breeding-year indicators, pre-manipulation day-0 rearing-nest brood size (rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size), and rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH). Uncertainty used a finite-sample-corrected one-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest. Because unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, this is a covariate-adjusted observational contrast and may retain residual baseline confounding.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_unmanipulated = 1 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 7 (unmanipulated rearing brood); reported coefficient is adjusted mean day-14 weight for enlarged minus unmanipulated

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Chick-level OLS fitted to all 3,720 measured chicks from 452 rearing nests and 497 natal nests. Fixed effects were the ordered assigned-competition score and breeding-year indicators (2001 reference; 2002 and 2003 indicators). Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by rear_nest_breed_ID and hatch_nest_breed_ID. Test statistic: t = -9.496410758921938; inferential df = 451, defined conservatively as min(452 rearing-nest clusters, 497 natal-nest clusters) - 1. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation with reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. No observations were excluded for missing model variables. The coefficient assumes a linear trend across the three ordered treatment categories and is reported in its native scale, mm per score unit.
rows.predictor: assigned_competition_score, constructed from rear_nest_trt as reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, and enlarged (code 5) = +1; coefficient is the day-14 tarsus-length change per one-category increase toward greater assigned sibling competition

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) modeled for 2,801 chicks from 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched. Chick-level OLS included breeding-year fixed effects. Uncertainty used a finite-sample-corrected one-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest. Test statistic: t = 11.35391099051841; inferential df = 331. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment. The native-scale coefficient is the adjusted mean day-14 weight difference in grams for reduced minus enlarged broods.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: 1 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood), 0 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient contrast is reduced minus enlarged

rows.note: Day-14 mass (grams) was modeled for 2,794 chicks in 331 rearing nests assigned to experimentally enlarged or reduced broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched. Seven otherwise eligible chicks were excluded by complete-case analysis of the adjustment variables. The fitted model was a maximum-likelihood Gaussian linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept for rearing nest. Fixed adjustments were a linear breeding-season trend (hatch_year minus its minimum), rearing-nest hatch date centered within breeding year, and pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size centered over the fitted sample. No post-treatment variable was adjusted for. The focal model-based Wald statistic was z = -11.723675862913653, with an asymptotic normal reference distribution and no finite inferential df. Observation unit: chick. Design: randomized brood-size manipulation contrast. Estimated rearing-nest random-intercept variance = 0.6142259162930687 g^2, residual variance = 0.5822200193982928 g^2, ICC = 0.5133754045795147.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced = 1 for chicks reared in experimentally enlarged broods (rear_nest_trt == 5) and 0 for chicks reared in experimentally reduced broods (rear_nest_trt == 6); coefficient is adjusted mean day-14 mass for enlarged minus reduced assignment

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) analyzed for 3,594 chicks with complete outcome, net manipulation dose, breeding year, rearing-nest clutch size, rearing-nest hatch date, and rearing/natal nest IDs; 126 of 3,720 rows were excluded for missing required values. Chick-level OLS modeled a linear dose response and adjusted for breeding-year fixed effects plus centered pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size and hatch date. Inference used a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust covariance matrix by 434 rearing nests and 477 natal nests. Test statistic: t = -12.19364208545086; inferential df = min(434,477)-1 = 433. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment including reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. The recorded dose ranged from -4 to +4 net chicks. The native coefficient is grams of day-14 weight per one net chick added; no effect-size conversion was applied.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation = rear_Cs_in minus rear_Cs_out, measured as net chicks added to the rearing brood (negative for reduction, 0 for no net manipulation, positive for enlargement); focal coefficient is the linear change in day-14 weight in grams per +1 net chick added

rows.note: Outcome: day-14 body mass (grams). Model: chick-level OLS, day_14_weight ~ assigned_competition_score + categorical hatch_year. The assigned competition score was constructed from rearing-nest treatment as reduced (rear_nest_trt=6) = -1, unmanipulated (rear_nest_trt=7) = 0, and enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5) = +1; its coefficient assumes a linear trend across these three categories. Dependence was handled using a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by rearing nest and natal/hatch nest. Test: t = -11.898944870634967; inferential df = 451, defined conservatively as min(452 rearing-nest clusters, 497 natal-nest clusters) - 1. Fitted n = 3,720 chicks, with no missing-data exclusions. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation with reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. Native effect: grams per one-unit increase in the ordered competition score; SE is also in grams per score unit.
rows.predictor: Assigned sibling-competition score: reduced rearing brood = -1, unmanipulated rearing brood = 0, enlarged rearing brood = +1; coefficient is the day-14 mass change per one-category increase toward greater competition.

rows.note: Outcome: rearing-brood mean day-14 weight (g). Analysis sample: experimentally manipulated broods only (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6) with observed nonzero net_rearing_manipulation and complete day-14 weight, year, and rearing-nest ID; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched, and missing/zero dose records were excluded. Annual rearing broods were identified by hatch_year plus rear_nest_breed_ID. Model: chick-count-weighted linear regression of brood-mean weight on signed net manipulation and breeding-year indicators, with HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance. Native effect = -0.167008 g per +1 chick; SE = 0.0145794 g; HC2 robust t = -11.4551; inferential df = 316. Fitted n = 320 annual rearing broods representing 2,716 measured chicks. Observation unit: annual rearing-brood mean. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation dose analysis. Aggregation handles dependence among chicks within rearing broods; natal-nest dependence across rearing broods was not explicitly modeled.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: recorded net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive for additions/enlargement, negative for removals/reduction), modeled linearly; coefficient is the change in mean day-14 weight per +1 chick

stats.unit: annual rearing-brood mean, identified by hatch_year plus rear_nest_breed_ID

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight (grams). Sample: 2,801 chicks measured at day 14 from 332 experimentally manipulated rearing nests; unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7 broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Model: Gaussian linear mixed-effects model fitted by maximum likelihood, day_14_weight ~ reduced_vs_enlarged + categorical hatch_year, with a random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment. Focal Wald z = 11.45002146884827; inferential df are not applicable for this asymptotic Wald z test. Estimated rearing-nest random-intercept variance = 0.6434231295972919 g^2; residual variance = 0.5841356239677495 g^2. The model converged.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: 1 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood), 0 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient is the adjusted reduced-minus-enlarged difference in mean day-14 weight

rows.note: Native effect: -1.0161397606101599 g; two-way cluster-robust SE: 0.08566504764594543 g. Test statistic: asymptotic z = -11.861777802422717; inferential df: not applicable (standard-normal inference for the two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance). Fitted n = 2,801 chicks; observation unit = chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment analyzed with chick-level OLS for day_14_weight, including breeding-year fixed effects, with covariance clustered jointly by 332 rearing nests and 377 natal nests using the two-way inclusion-exclusion sandwich estimator with finite-cluster covariance corrections. Analysis included experimentally enlarged and reduced broods and excluded unmanipulated broods because those were not systematically matched. No post-treatment brood-size or survival variables were adjusted for. The focal coefficient is the adjusted mean day-14 mass difference in grams for enlarged minus reduced rearing broods.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced = 1 if rear_nest_trt == 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 if rear_nest_trt == 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

rows.note: Outcome: supplied day_14_weight/(day_14_tarsus_length^2), a size-indexed day-14 body-condition proxy in g/mm^2. OLS marginal model included the enlarged-versus-reduced indicator and breeding-year fixed effects. Inference used a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest and hatch nest. Two-sided t = -8.5170540355 with inferential df = 331, defined as the smaller cluster count minus 1. Fitted n = 2,801 individual chicks measured at day 14, comprising 332 rearing-nest and 377 hatch-nest clusters. Design: experimental enlarged-versus-reduced rearing-brood comparison. Unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods; rows missing model variables would also be excluded. No post-treatment covariates were included. Native effect and SE remain in g/mm^2.
rows.predictor: Indicator equal to 1 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced contrast.

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight (grams). Maximum-likelihood linear mixed model fitted to 3,679 chicks with complete required data (41 excluded for missing rear_nest_CS or rear_nest_OH), from 447 rearing nests and 491 natal nests. Fixed effects were the assigned sibling-competition score, centered numeric hatch year (linear temporal trend), centered pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size, and centered rearing-nest hatch date. Cross-classified random intercepts modeled dependence within rearing nests and natal nests. Random-intercept variances were 0.53123 (rearing nest) and 0.16268 (natal nest); residual variance was 0.46842. The focal model-based Wald statistic was z = -12.0465, with asymptotic inference and no finite inferential df. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear ordered trend across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods; inclusion of the unmatched unmanipulated group relies on baseline covariate adjustment and the assumed linear category trend.
rows.predictor: Assigned sibling-competition score coded -1 for experimentally reduced rearing broods, 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods, and +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods; coefficient is grams of day-14 mass per one-category increase in this score.

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GEE for day-14 weight (grams), with exchangeable working correlation within rearing nest and robust sandwich SE. Included reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods; complete cases for outcome, treatment, year, rearing-nest hatch date, clutch size, and rearing-nest ID. Adjusted for a linear breeding-season trend (hatch_year minus its minimum), rearing-nest hatch date centered within breeding year, and pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size centered over the fitted sample. Fitted n=3,679 chicks from 447 rearing nests; observation unit=chick; design=brood-size manipulation experiment, noting that unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Native effect=-0.5425327384 grams per one-step increase in the specified competition score; robust SE=0.0458606312 grams per step. Test statistic: t=-11.83003208; inferential df=442, defined as 447 rearing-nest clusters minus 5 fitted parameters. The score imposes equal spacing across the three categories; no post-treatment variables were adjusted for.
rows.predictor: One-step increase in ordered sibling-competition score coded reduced brood = -1, unmanipulated brood = 0, enlarged brood = +1; coefficient is the fitted linear grams-per-step slope across all three groups.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Fitted chick-level OLS on all 3,720 chicks with nominal three-level rear_nest_trt (decoded as reduced, unmanipulated, enlarged) and breeding-year fixed effects; no observations were excluded for missing required values. The focal planned contrast was enlarged minus the equally weighted mean of reduced and unmanipulated adjusted group means. Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by rearing nest (452 clusters) and natal/hatch nest (497 clusters). Native effect = -0.3220674081 mm; SE = 0.0403115971 mm; t = -7.989447984; inferential df = min(452,497)-1 = 451. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation with enlarged, reduced, and unmanipulated rearing broods; treatment modeled categorically without a linear-spacing assumption.
rows.predictor: Planned signed contrast of breeding-year-adjusted treatment means: mean(day-14 tarsus length | experimentally enlarged rearing brood) - 0.5*[mean(day-14 tarsus length | experimentally reduced rearing brood) + mean(day-14 tarsus length | unmanipulated rearing brood)]

rows.note: Native effect: grams of day-14 weight per one-chick increase in signed net rearing manipulation. Robust GEE test: t = -12.2906179494 with inferential df = 313 (318 rearing-nest clusters minus 5 fitted parameters). Fitted n = 2,709 chicks; observation unit = chick. Design/sample: brood-size manipulation experiment restricted to experimentally enlarged and reduced rearing broods with complete modeled fields; unmanipulated broods were excluded. Model: Gaussian identity-link GEE with exchangeable within-rearing-nest working correlation and robust sandwich SE. Adjustments: linear breeding-season trend, rearing-nest hatch date centered within breeding year, and centered pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size. The focal predictor was modeled linearly over observed values -4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4; records missing manipulation magnitude or adjustment variables were excluded. The estimate means 0.1825 g lower day-14 mass per additional chick added by the manipulation.
rows.predictor: net_chicks_added = net_rearing_manipulation, coded as the signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (negative for reductions, positive for enlargements); focal coefficient is the change in day-14 weight per +1 chick

rows.note: Day-14 tarsus length (mm) was regressed at the chick level on net_rearing_manipulation and breeding-year fixed indicators using OLS. The focal dose was modeled linearly. Two-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance accounted for dependence within rearing nests and natal nests. Uncertainty used t inference with df=min(439 rearing-nest clusters, 483 natal-nest clusters)-1=438: t=-9.274697528984639. Fitted n=3,635 chicks (observation unit: individual chick) from 439 rearing nests and 483 natal nests; 85 rows were excluded because net_rearing_manipulation was missing. Brood-size manipulation design included reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods; observed dose range was -4 to +4. No adjustment was made for clutch size, hatch date, realized brood size, survival, or other post-treatment variables.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation = rear_Cs_in minus rear_Cs_out, measured as net chicks added to the rearing brood (negative=reduced, 0=unmanipulated, positive=enlarged); coefficient is mm of day-14 tarsus length per one net chick added

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Model: chick-level OLS with rear_nest_trt represented as a nominal three-level factor (5=enlarged, 6=reduced, 7=unmanipulated) and breeding-year fixed indicators (2001 reference; 2002 and 2003 indicators). No covariates beyond breeding year and no missing-data exclusions were used. Fitted n=3,720 chicks: 1,742 enlarged, 1,059 reduced, and 919 unmanipulated; observation unit=individual chick; design=brood-size manipulation experiment including all three rearing-brood groups. Dependence was handled using a crossed-cluster multiplier bootstrap with independent Exp(1) weights for 452 rearing nests and 497 natal nests, multiplied at chick level; 2,000 replicates, random seed 20250308. The reported SE is the bootstrap SD. Native-scale Wald statistic: z=-5.034663008785264; inferential df=not applicable (asymptotic normal test with bootstrap SE); two-sided p=4.786901869372605e-07. The estimate means enlarged broods had adjusted day-14 tarsus length 0.3221 mm lower than the equally weighted average of reduced and unmanipulated broods.
rows.predictor: Signed planned contrast of breeding-year-adjusted treatment means: mean(day-14 tarsus length | enlarged rearing brood) - 0.5*[mean(day-14 tarsus length | reduced rearing brood) + mean(day-14 tarsus length | unmanipulated rearing brood)]

rows.note: Outcome: day-14 body mass (grams). Model: chick-level ordinary least squares with the ordered assigned sibling-competition score, categorical breeding-year fixed effects, and categorical molecular-sex adjustment. Analysis used complete cases requiring observed mass, treatment category, year, molecular sex, rearing-nest ID, and natal-nest ID: fitted n=2,626 chicks; 1,094 of 3,720 measured chicks were excluded because molecular sex was missing. Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by 327 rearing nests and 354 natal nests. Native focal effect=-0.51979698 grams per one-score-unit increase; SE=0.04999623 grams. Test statistic: t=-10.39672381; inferential df=326, defined conservatively as min(327 rearing-nest clusters, 354 natal-nest clusters)-1. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear trend over reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. The model assumes equal incremental effects from reduced to unmanipulated and from unmanipulated to enlarged. Sex codes 1 and 2 were treated categorically without assigning biological labels.
rows.predictor: Assigned sibling-competition score constructed from rear_nest_trt as reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, and enlarged (code 5) = +1; coefficient is the adjusted change in day-14 mass in grams per +1 category step toward greater competition.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Model: chick-level OLS with a linear effect of rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, adjusted for categorical hatch_year, centered pre-manipulation rear_nest_CS, and centered rear_nest_OH. Two-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance accounted for dependence within rearing nests and natal nests. Focal test: t = -11.998639852897623 with inferential df = 393, defined as min(394 rearing-nest clusters, 437 natal-nest clusters) - 1. Fitted n = 3292 chicks; observation unit = individual chick; 428 rows were excluded for missing values in the outcome, exposure, adjustment variables, or cluster IDs. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment analyzed using absolute post-manipulation starting rearing-brood size, which combines experimentally induced and naturally occurring brood-size variation; thus this conditional dose association is not solely an intention-to-treat effect. Exposure range was 2 to 18 chicks. The estimate and SE are in grams per additional chick in the starting rearing brood.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing: absolute number of chicks in the rearing brood immediately after manipulation; focal signed quantity is a +1-chick increase in starting rearing-brood size

rows.note: Outcome was mean day-14 weight (grams) among measured chicks within each year-specific rearing nest, defined by the composite key (hatch_year, rear_nest_breed_ID). The fitted sample comprised 333 experimentally manipulated rearing-nest seasons representing 2,801 chicks; unmanipulated broods (rear_nest_trt=7) were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. I fitted equal-brood-weighted OLS with separate breeding-year intercepts and HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance across brood-seasons. Aggregation to one mean per brood-season handled within-rearing-nest dependence. Focal Wald t=11.567477412576956 with 329 residual inferential df (two-sided p=3.386998815679419e-26); 95% CI [0.8996573028001061, 1.268356354040712] grams. Observation unit: year-specific rearing-nest mean. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation, reduced versus enlarged broods. The native effect is the adjusted brood-average difference in day-14 weight, in grams.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: 1 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood), 0 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient is reduced minus enlarged

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) modeled for 2,801 chicks from 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Gaussian linear mixed model fitted by REML with breeding-year fixed effects and a normally distributed random intercept for rearing nest to model within-brood dependence. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment. Focal Wald z = -11.382036445429671; inferential df are not applicable because the model-based test uses asymptotic normal inference. No post-treatment brood-size, survival, manipulation-magnitude, natal-nest, or derived body-condition variables were included.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator equal to 1 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced in mean day-14 weight

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Gaussian identity-link GEE fitted to all 3,720 chicks, with breeding-year fixed effects and an exchangeable working correlation within 452 rearing nests; robust sandwich uncertainty. Estimated exchangeable working correlation=0.322468. Focal test: asymptotic z=-8.702837; inferential df not applicable. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation including reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. No observations were excluded for missing required model variables. The coefficient assumes a linear trend across the three ordered treatment categories and is the change in day-14 tarsus length per one-category increase in assigned competition; it is not the full enlarged-minus-reduced difference.
rows.predictor: Assigned sibling-competition score constructed from rear_nest_trt as reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, and enlarged (code 5) = +1; coefficient is mm of day-14 tarsus length per +1 score unit.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Model: unadjusted chick-level OLS, day_14_weight ~ reduced_vs_enlarged, using only experimentally manipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6); unmatched unmanipulated broods (code 7) were excluded. No adjustment variables were included. Uncertainty used a one-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance by rearing_nest_breed_ID. Test: t = 11.334902455044917 with 331 inferential df (332 rearing-nest clusters minus 1), two-sided p = 2.1954437818565935e-25. Fitted n = 2801 chicks; observation unit = chick; 332 rearing nests. Design: experimental rearing-brood enlargement/reduction through cross-fostering. The native coefficient is reduced minus enlarged, so reduced broods averaged 1.01408 g heavier at day 14.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient is the reduced-minus-enlarged mean day-14 weight contrast

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Fitted chick-level OLS among experimentally enlarged and reduced broods, adjusted linearly for post-manipulation rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, pre-treatment rear_nest_CS, and rear_nest_OH; no breeding-year fixed effects and no realized day-14 brood-size adjustment. Unmanipulated broods and rows missing any fitted variable were excluded. Finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust covariance accounted for rearing and hatch nests. Wald t = -0.5760044034608013 with conservative df = min(321 rearing nests, 364 hatch nests) - 1 = 320; two-sided p = 0.565017076463842. Fitted n = 2727 individual chicks alive and measured at day 14. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation with cross-fostering. This is a conditional enlarged-versus-reduced contrast at equal post-manipulation starting brood size, clutch size, and hatch date, not the total assignment effect.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced indicator: 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood), 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Native effect: -0.5430291257 grams of mean day-14 weight per one-step increase in the competition score; SE 0.04729071846 grams per score step. Wald t = -11.48278443 with 449 residual inferential df. Fitted n = 453 year-specific rearing-nest seasons, formed from 3,720 chicks. Observation unit: the mean day-14 chick weight within each hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID brood-season; brood-seasons were equally weighted. Design/model: OLS linear trend across all three rearing-brood categories, with separate breeding-year intercepts and HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance across brood-seasons. Treatment decoding was 5=enlarged, 6=reduced, 7=unmanipulated. No outcome observations were missing. The model imposes equal linear spacing across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged categories; unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, so that component is not as securely randomized as the manipulated comparison.
rows.predictor: competition_score = -1 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced), 0 for rear_nest_trt 7 (unmanipulated), and +1 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged); coefficient is the change in brood-season mean day-14 weight, in grams, per one-category increase toward greater sibling competition

stats.unit: year-specific rearing-nest season mean of day-14 chick weight

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day-14 weight (grams). Model: chick-level ordinary least squares with net_rearing_manipulation as a linear continuous dose, adjusted for centered linear hatch year, centered pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size (rear_nest_CS), and centered rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH). Complete-case fitted n=3,594 chicks; 126 of 3,720 rows were excluded for missing net manipulation or another required model variable. Fitted sample contained 434 rearing nests and 477 natal nests. Dependence from both nest classifications was handled by a crossed pigeonhole bootstrap: in each of 2,000 replicates (seed 20250308), rearing nests and natal nests were independently multinomial-resampled, their cluster weights were multiplied for each chick, and weighted least squares was refitted. All 2,000 replicates were valid; the reported SE is the bootstrap SD of focal coefficients. Native effect=-0.1774103102 grams per net chick added; SE=0.0222435932 grams per net chick added. Test statistic: asymptotic Wald z=-7.9757937; inferential df not applicable; two-sided p=1.5140e-15. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI: [-0.2218196, -0.1333516]. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation/cross-fostering experiment analyzed as a continuous net manipulation dose, including reduced, zero-net/unmanipulated, and enlarged broods with recorded dose. The linear dose-response assumption is explicit.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation = net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (chicks moved in minus chicks moved out as recorded): negative for reductions, 0 for no net change, positive for enlargements; fitted range -4 to +4; coefficient is grams of day-14 weight per 1 additional net chick

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Focal model: chick-level OLS with a linear effect of rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, adjusted for categorical hatch_year, centered rear_nest_CS, and centered rear_nest_OH. Missing rearing-nest predictors were handled with 20 posterior-draw iterative imputations performed on one row per rearing nest, using hatch year, treatment category, clutch size, hatch date, recorded day-0 rearing brood size, net rearing manipulation, starting rearing brood size, and rearing-nest mean day-14 weight as imputation variables; imputed analysis variables were bounded to observed ranges and then merged back to chicks. This retained all 3,720 chicks from 452 rearing nests and 497 natal nests; 53 nests had missing starting brood size and 5 had missing clutch size. Each imputed fit used two-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest and natal nest. Coefficients and variances were pooled with Rubin's rules. Native effect = -0.0885921 g per additional chick; pooled SE = 0.0175068 g; t = -5.06042; inferential df = 115.667 from Rubin's rules (below the cluster df cap of 451). Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation study analyzed as a linear absolute-starting-brood-size exposure; this exposure combines experimentally induced and naturally occurring brood-size variation.
rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing: absolute number of chicks in the rearing brood immediately after manipulation; coefficient is the change in day-14 weight (g) per one additional chick

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length in millimetres, fit with an identity-link linear model. Analysis: unadjusted chick-level OLS restricted to 2,801 chicks in experimentally manipulated broods (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6); unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. No adjustment variables were included. Uncertainty used a one-way finite-sample-corrected cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest (332 clusters). Test statistic: t = 8.173049703272437; inferential df = 331. Observation unit: chick. Design: experimental rearing-brood-size manipulation. The estimate is the mean day-14 tarsus-length difference in mm for reduced minus enlarged broods.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged = 1 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient is reduced minus enlarged

rows.note: Native effect: grams of day-14 weight per one-unit increase in signed net chicks added. Test: t = -12.372406154387342 with inferential df = 431 (439 rearing-nest clusters minus 8 fitted parameters). Fitted n = 3,635 chicks; observation unit = chick; 439 rearing nests comprising 160 enlarged, 159 reduced, and 120 unmanipulated nests. Design/model: brood-size manipulation analyzed with a Gaussian identity-link GEE, exchangeable working correlation within rearing nest, and robust sandwich SE. Adjustments were a linear breeding-season trend, rearing-nest hatch date centered within year, centered pre-manipulation clutch size, missingness indicators with median filling for those adjustment variables, and a separate unmanipulated-brood indicator because controls were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Unmanipulated broods were assigned net manipulation 0. Manipulated broods lacking a recorded or exactly reconstructible signed manipulation were excluded (13 nests; 85 chicks); no missing net values were recoverable from chicks-in minus chicks-out bookkeeping. The focal model assumes a linear dose-response over observed net manipulations from -4 to +4 chicks. The negative estimate means one additional chick imposed by the manipulation is associated with 0.1827 g lower day-14 mass, conditional on the stated adjustments.
rows.predictor: net_chicks_added = net_rearing_manipulation in experimentally enlarged/reduced broods (signed number of chicks added: -4 to -1 for reductions and +1 to +4 for enlargements), with 0 assigned to unmanipulated broods; focal coefficient is the linear change in day-14 weight per +1 net chick added, while a separate unmanipulated indicator allows controls their own intercept

rows.note: Day-14 weight was averaged within each year-specific rearing nest, defined by (hatch_year, rear_nest_breed_ID), and each brood-season was weighted equally. OLS regressed brood-season mean day-14 weight (grams) on continuous net_rearing_manipulation and separate breeding-year intercepts, with HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance across brood-seasons. Brood-seasons missing net_rearing_manipulation were excluded. Fitted n = 440 brood-seasons representing 3,635 chicks; observed manipulation range = -4 to +4 net chicks. Native focal effect = -0.1824154843 grams per net chick added; SE = 0.0154521226 grams per net chick added. Test statistic: t = -11.80520561; inferential df = 436. Observation unit: year-specific rearing-nest mean. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear continuous manipulation-dose association, with breeding-season-specific intercepts and HC2 uncertainty. The linear per-chick interpretation assumes comparability of manipulation magnitudes, which were scaled to initial brood size.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation = rear_Cs_in minus rear_Cs_out for the rearing brood (negative when chicks were removed, zero when unchanged, positive when chicks were added); coefficient is the change in brood-season mean day-14 weight in grams per one additional net chick added

rows.note: Outcome: mean day-14 weight (grams) within each rearing brood, where brood identity was constructed as hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID to prevent IDs reused across years from being merged. Included all 453 broods assigned to reduced, unmanipulated, or enlarged categories, representing 3,720 measured chicks; no outcome observations were missing. Fitted chick-count-weighted least squares of brood-mean weight on the ordered competition score plus breeding-year indicators, with HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance. Native effect = grams per +1 score step; robust t = -11.2956697032 with 449 residual df. Observation unit: year-specific rearing brood. Design: brood-size manipulation including all three assigned categories. The ordered model assumes equally spaced, linear effects across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged categories. Unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, and natal-nest dependence was not explicitly modeled.
rows.predictor: Assigned sibling-competition score constructed from rear_nest_trt: reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, enlarged (code 5) = +1; coefficient is per one-unit increase toward greater assigned competition.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Gaussian identity-link GEE fitted to all 3,720 chicks from 452 rearing nests, with nominal rear_nest_trt category and breeding-year fixed effects. Treatment decoding: code 5=enlarged, code 6=reduced, code 7=unmanipulated. Unmanipulated was the reference; separate reduced and enlarged indicators avoided imposing a linear trend, and the reduced group remained in the model. Dependence among chicks in the same rearing nest was modeled with an exchangeable working correlation (estimated correlation 0.3197836); uncertainty used the robust GEE sandwich covariance. Focal robust SE=0.05503568 mm; asymptotic z=-4.87583547; inferential df=not applicable; fitted n=3,720 chicks; observation unit=chick; design=brood-size manipulation analyzed across enlarged, reduced, and unmanipulated rearing broods. No observations were excluded for missing required variables. Caveat: unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, so the enlarged-minus-unmanipulated contrast may retain baseline group differences.
rows.predictor: Nominal treatment contrast 1(enlarged rearing brood) - 1(unmanipulated rearing brood), conditional on a separate reduced-brood indicator and breeding-year indicators; enlarged minus unmanipulated.

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GEE of day-14 weight (grams) on net chicks added, fitted to 3,594 chicks in 434 rearing nests from the brood-size manipulation. Exchangeable working correlation modeled dependence within rearing nest; robust sandwich SE was used (estimated working correlation 0.5473). Adjusted for a linear breeding-season trend (hatch_year minus its minimum), rearing-nest hatch date centered within breeding year, and pre-manipulation rearing-nest clutch size centered over the fitted sample. Complete-case exclusions applied to outcome, net manipulation, hatch year, hatch date, clutch size, and rearing-nest ID; no post-treatment variables were adjusted for. Net manipulation ranged from -4 to +4. Native-scale test: t = -12.225664, inferential df = 429 (434 rearing-nest clusters minus 5 fitted parameters), two-sided p = 1.0711e-29. Observation unit: chick. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged broods. The model assumes a linear mass difference per net chick added.
rows.predictor: net_chicks_added = numeric net_rearing_manipulation: number of chicks moved into minus number moved out of the rearing brood; focal coefficient is the linear change in day-14 weight (grams) for +1 net chick added

rows.note: Day-14 chick weight was averaged within each season-specific rearing brood, identified by (hatch_year, rear_nest_breed_ID). Equal-weight brood-level OLS was fitted to 333 broods (167 enlarged, 166 reduced; sourced from 2,801 chicks), with breeding-year fixed effects and HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust uncertainty. Unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Native effect = -1.0840068 g, SE = 0.0937116 g; t = -11.5674774 with 329 residual df. Observation unit: season-specific rearing brood. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation. Outcome: within-brood mean day-14 weight in grams.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood), 0 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the enlarged-minus-reduced contrast in brood-mean day-14 chick weight

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) was modeled for 2,727 chicks in manipulated broods using OLS with categorical breeding year and original rearing-nest clutch size as covariates. Uncertainty used a two-way cluster-robust covariance by rearing nest (321 clusters) and natal nest (364 clusters). The cluster-robust t statistic was -12.1102463098 with conservative inferential df = min(321, 364) - 1 = 320. Observation unit: individual chick measured at day 14. Design: brood-size manipulation dose analysis. Unmanipulated broods and records missing outcome, post-manipulation starting brood size, original clutch size, year, or nest IDs, or having nonpositive size values, were excluded. Native effect scale: grams per one-unit increase in log relative brood size.
rows.predictor: ln(rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing / rear_nest_CS): natural log of brood size immediately after manipulation divided by original rearing-nest clutch size; coefficient is per one-unit increase in this log ratio (an e-fold increase in the ratio), with positive values indicating proportionally greater sibling competition

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight in grams. Model: chick-level OLS, day_14_weight ~ assigned_competition_score + categorical hatch_year + categorical sex_adjustment. Molecular sex codes 1 and 2 were retained as separate categories, and missing molecular sex was retained as an explicit 'unknown' category (not biologically imputed). Predictor score was constructed from rear_nest_trt as reduced (code 6) = -1, unmanipulated (code 7) = 0, enlarged (code 5) = +1; the coefficient assumes a linear trend and is grams per one-category increase. Required non-sex fields were outcome, treatment, year, rearing-nest ID, and natal-nest ID; none were missing, so fitted n=3,720 chicks. Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by 452 rearing nests and 497 natal nests. Test statistic: t=-11.758624450406643; inferential df=451, defined conservatively as min(number of rearing-nest clusters, number of natal-nest clusters)-1. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods, with breeding-year adjustment.
rows.predictor: assigned sibling-competition score: rear_nest_trt 6 (reduced) = -1, rear_nest_trt 7 (unmanipulated) = 0, rear_nest_trt 5 (enlarged) = +1; effect per +1 score unit

rows.note: Unadjusted Gaussian identity-link GEE of day-14 weight (grams) on an intercept and net chicks added, with exchangeable working correlation within rearing nest and robust sandwich SE. Complete cases for day_14_weight, net_rearing_manipulation, and rear_nest_breed_ID were used; fitted n=3,635 chicks in 439 rearing nests. Observation unit: chick. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation, including reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged broods with observed net manipulation from -4 to +4 chicks. No adjustment covariates and no post-treatment variables were included. The focal coefficient assumes a linear response per net chick added. Test statistic: t=-11.9062943510; inferential df=437, defined as 439 rearing-nest clusters minus 2 fitted parameters. Native effect and SE are in grams per net chick added.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation used as a continuous signed quantity: net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (chicks moved in minus chicks moved out), ranging from -4 to +4; focal effect is the change in day-14 weight for a +1 chick increment

rows.note: Outcome: within-rearing-nest mean day-14 tarsus length (mm), modeled by identity-link OLS. Sample: 332 experimentally manipulated rearing nests (167 enlarged, 165 reduced), containing 2,801 measured chicks; unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. No adjustment variables were included. Uncertainty used HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance across the independent rearing-nest observations. Test: t = 8.394986910774202 with 330 residual df (two-sided p = 1.3912697162025998e-15). Fitted n = 332; observation unit = rearing nest. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment analyzed as an equal-rearing-brood comparison.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: 1 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced brood), 0 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged brood); coefficient is reduced minus enlarged

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length (mm), modeled with an identity-link linear regression. Focal test: t = -8.130411181448082 with 318 inferential df (319 rearing-nest clusters minus 1). Fitted n = 2716 chicks; observation unit = chick. Design/sample: brood-size manipulation, restricted to experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods with nonmissing net_rearing_manipulation; unmanipulated broods and missing doses excluded. Model: unadjusted chick-level OLS with no adjustment variables and a finite-sample-corrected one-way cluster-robust covariance matrix by rear_nest_breed_ID. The observed predictor range was -4 to +4 chicks, and the coefficient assumes a linear effect per one-chick increment.
rows.predictor: competition_dose = net_rearing_manipulation, the signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (chicks moved in minus chicks moved out); coefficient is the change in day-14 tarsus length in mm per +1 net chick added

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_weight (grams). Fitted n=3,720 chicks; observation unit=individual chick; 452 rearing nests and 497 natal nests; no exclusions for required fields. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as an ordered linear trend across reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged rearing broods. Model: linear regression with natal-nest fixed effects absorbed by within-natal-nest demeaning; adjusted for molecular sex (code 1, code 2, or an explicit unknown category) and breeding-year indicators. Dependence remaining within rearing nests was handled with a finite-sample-corrected one-way rearing-nest cluster-robust sandwich covariance; the correction counted the 497 absorbed natal-nest effects and the transformed-design rank (full rank 501). Of the natal nests, 275 had within-nest competition-score variation. Test statistic: t=-14.768111969359031; inferential df=451 (452 rearing clusters minus 1). The estimate and SE are on the native gram scale and assume a linear effect per one-category increase in the ordered score.
rows.predictor: assigned sibling-competition score constructed exactly as reduced rearing brood = -1, unmanipulated rearing brood = 0, enlarged rearing brood = +1; coefficient is grams of day-14 mass per +1 score unit

rows.note: Day-14 weight (grams) modeled for 2,716 chicks from 319 experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods with complete data. Gaussian identity-link GEE used an exchangeable working correlation within rearing nest and robust sandwich SE. The model adjusted for categorical hatch year and centered pre-manipulation day-0 rearing-nest brood size; unmanipulated broods and rows missing modeled variables were excluded. Native focal effect = -0.183553 g per net chick added; robust SE = 0.0147765 g per net chick added. Test statistic: t = -12.42199; inferential df = 314, defined as 319 rearing-nest clusters minus 5 fitted parameters. Observation unit: chick. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment, analyzed as a signed manipulation-dose response. The linear focal term assumes a constant effect per chick across observed net manipulations from -4 to +4 (zero was absent because unmanipulated broods were excluded).
rows.predictor: net_chicks_added = net_rearing_manipulation, entered linearly in units of chicks; observed values -4, -3, -2, -1, +1, +2, +3, +4. The coefficient is the change in day-14 weight (grams) for a +1-chick increase in signed net rearing-brood manipulation.

rows.note: Outcome: day_14_tarsus_length in millimetres. Sample: 2,801 chicks measured at day 14 from 332 experimentally manipulated rearing nests; unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7 broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Model: Gaussian linear mixed-effects model fitted by maximum likelihood using BFGS; fixed effects were reduced_vs_enlarged and categorical hatch_year (2001 reference, with 2002 and 2003 indicators); a random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID modeled within-rearing-nest dependence. The BFGS fit converged without warnings. Cross-optimizer diagnostics (L-BFGS, BFGS, Powell, CG) gave essentially identical estimates, SEs, likelihoods, and variance components; the Hessian was nonsingular. Native focal effect = 0.3811689 mm, model-based SE = 0.0446516 mm; Wald z = 8.5365; inferential df not applicable; observation unit = chick; design = brood-size manipulation experiment. Estimated rearing-nest random-intercept variance was 0.1221439 mm^2 and residual variance was 0.3134633 mm^2.
rows.predictor: reduced_vs_enlarged: indicator equal to 1 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood); coefficient is adjusted mean day-14 tarsus length for reduced minus enlarged broods

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_tarsus_length (mm) among measured day-14 chicks within each rearing nest. Model: equal-weight, unadjusted rearing-nest-level OLS with identity link and HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust covariance. Test: t = -8.49742019115113 with 317 inferential df. Fitted n = 319 rearing-nest means, derived from 2,716 chicks. Observation unit: rearing nest. Design: brood-size manipulation; included experimentally enlarged and reduced broods with observed net_rearing_manipulation; excluded unmanipulated broods and manipulated broods missing that dose. No adjustment variables. Exposure range was -4 to +4 net chicks. The estimate is the change in mean day-14 tarsus length, in mm, per one-chick increase in signed net manipulation.
rows.predictor: competition_dose = net_rearing_manipulation, constructed as the signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (chicks moved in minus chicks moved out); focal effect is per +1 net chick added

rows.note: Outcome: day-14 body mass (grams). Model: chick-level ordinary least squares with assigned rearing-brood treatment represented as an unrestricted three-level categorical factor and breeding-year fixed effects (2001 reference; indicators for 2002 and 2003). Focal contrast: adjusted mean for enlarged broods minus one-half the sum of the adjusted means for reduced and unmanipulated broods. Dependence was handled with a finite-sample-corrected two-way cluster-robust sandwich covariance by rearing nest and hatch/natal nest. No required values were missing: fitted n=3,720 chicks, comprising 1,742 enlarged, 1,059 reduced, and 919 unmanipulated chicks; 452 rearing-nest clusters and 497 natal-nest clusters. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation with cross-fostering, including enlarged, reduced, and unmanipulated rearing broods. Native effect=-0.9642511829 g; SE=0.0863284731 g. Test statistic: t=-11.16956142; inferential df=451, conservatively defined as min(452 rearing clusters, 497 natal clusters)-1; two-sided p=9.6784e-26. The contrast does not impose a linear trend or equal spacing among treatment groups.
rows.predictor: Assigned rearing-brood treatment categorical contrast: mean(day-14 mass | enlarged) - 0.5*[mean(day-14 mass | reduced) + mean(day-14 mass | unmanipulated)], conditional on breeding year
